messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [SEV-2] High error-rate alert for tenant acme-inc. 500s spiking to 32% over 5m. Routing-service reports unexpected spillover from dedicated pool to hosted pool and repeated region fallback attempts. Auto-created thread for triage.

samir: I'm on it — paging eng-sre and eng-platform. @maya @elaine can you join the call?

maya: joining. seeing repeated log lines: route_eval matched capacity-tier override -> spillover=true for tenant_id=acme-inc region=eu-west-1 even though dedicated pool reported available capacity.

elaine: i'm looking at recent routing-service deploy at 2026-03-15T11:12Z (deploy id deploy-20260315-1128, PR #2389). PR changed comparator ordering in policy evaluation. Investigating revert now.

jord: logs snippet from routing-service: 
```
[11:22:43] route_eval info tenant=acme-inc policy=capacity-tier match=true spillover=true target_pool=hosted
[11:22:44] kvcache error miss tenant=acme-inc model_variant=gpt-small-quant fallback=region-loop
[11:22:46] route_eval warn tenant=acme-inc fallback=eu-central -> re-eval -> spillover=true
```

samir: can we disable spillover for acme-inc quickly to stop the leak?

jord: running runtime command to disable: 
```
redwood routes update --tenant acme-inc --set spillover=false --auth-token=$INFER_OPS_TOKEN
```

jord: command applied (exit 0). Confirmed policy now returns spillover=false for acme-inc on current evals.

incident-bot: automated action: routing-service rollback to v1.3.7 initiated by elaine.

maya: metrics update — error-rate down to ~1.1% over last 3m. Latency SLO for dedicated pool restored. However, we observed some requests were routed to a wrong model variant (gpt-small-quant) during the spillover window causing quality regressions for ~12 minutes.

elaine: preliminary root cause: PR #2389 changed comparator priority so that region_fallback was evaluated before capacity-tier checks. Combined with an edge tenant tag (allow_spill) the policy incorrectly decided spillover was the correct action and then region fallback caused alternating routing between eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 (loop), which then matched hosted pool rules.

samir: customer impact summary for CS: acme-inc (dedicated) experienced degraded responses and model-variant regressions for ~12 minutes starting ~11:21Z, approx 4k requests affected. Immediate mitigation done at ~11:33Z. Please prepare a note for Acme success manager.

cs-liaison-bot: @cs-team notification sent: impacted customers: acme-inc (primary), beta-corp (partial). Slack DM to acme-success-manager queued.

maya: mitigation checklist I used: 1) disable tenant spillover via runtime API, 2) rollback routing-service to stable v1.3.7, 3) pin acme-inc to dedicated pool for 30m, 4) sanity-run traffic replay to validate.

elaine: follow-ups and action items: 
- revert PR #2389 permanently and open a safe-revert PR with tests (owner: elaine)
- add regression tests for comparator ordering and tenant tag precedence (owner: maya)
- implement runtime circuit-breaker preventing spillover when dedicated pool isn't reporting >70% SLO violations (owner: jord)
- product to review routing policy UX so 'allow_spill' semantics are clearer (owner: @product)

samir: assigning and setting severity to SEV-2. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD today.

pagerduty: PagerDuty handoff scheduled to samir until 12:00Z, then elaine will take primary.

samir: handing off to elaine at 11:50Z. elaine — you own the postmortem and customer comms. :white_check_mark:

elaine: ack — will produce a blameless postmortem, include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and plans for preventive tests. I'll also coordinate an incident review with eng-platform and product.

maya: noted a small gap: routing telemetry didn't emit an explicit 'spillover decision' tag in every eval which made root-cause slower to surface. Adding that to telemetry backlog.

samir: thanks all. quick wins captured. we'll escalate to on-call rotation docs so next person can run a one-command mitigation: 
```
# Mitigation playbook snippet
# 1) Disable spillover
redwood routes update --tenant <tenant-id> --set spillover=false
# 2) Pin to dedicated for 30m
redwood routes pin --tenant <tenant-id> --pool dedicated --ttl 30m
# 3) Roll back routing-service if config deploy is suspected
kubectl -n routing rollout undo deployment/routing-service --to-revision=stable
```

jord: added guard in repo: routing-service now checks for "spillover if dedicated overloaded" and refuses to enable spillover when dedicated shows <70% error/latency breach in last 5m. Test PR opened.

cs-liaison-bot: update sent to acme-success-manager: summary, mitigation steps taken, ETA for postmortem.

samir: closing loop for now. Will convert thread into incident doc and link to postmortem when ready. React with :thumbsup: if no further immediate action.

elaine: :thumbsup: will own the writeup.

incident-bot: incident archived to incidents-tracker id INC-20260315-042."
